methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Robotics & Manufacturing (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 10 same-sector peers exist in Robotics & Manufacturing, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
OSH Cut, a bootstrapped robotics and manufacturing company founded by Caleb Chamberlain and Jacom Chamberlain, presents a valuation challenge due to its early stage and limited comparable universe. The sector comprises ten peers in Robotics & Manufacturing, including eight private companies such as Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, Generalist AI, and Bedrock Robotics, alongside a single public comparable (277810.KQ). However, the peer-median method is not applicable here: while the broader sector contains sufficient companies, filtering for same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-valuation-tier peers yields fewer than three datapoints—the minimum threshold for reliable triangulation.

This data scarcity precludes standard comparable-company analysis. Falling back to all-sector median multiples would introduce substantial bias given OSH Cut's bootstrapped status versus later-stage peers. Without sufficient same-stage or valuation-tier peers, revenue or EBITDA multiples derived from the broader peer set lack credibility for early-stage extrapolation.

A complete valuation therefore cannot be supported by the available data. To proceed, additional methods—such as discounted cash flow modeling (if financial projections exist), venture method frameworks, or identification of true seed-stage robotics comparables—would be necessary. The key uncertainty is OSH Cut's revenue traction and growth trajectory relative to the identified private peers, which remain unknown from this dataset.
